title: File descriptors are owned resources, not casual integers
summary: Descriptors created, accepted or received by the library are modeled as owned resources with close-on-exec discipline. Foreign Runtime owns POSIX_FD handles and UnixDescriptor provides explicit ownership transfer forms.
invariants: socket() and accept4() results are owned ForeignHandle POSIX_FD resources with close as destructor.
Created, accepted, socket-pair and received descriptors are close-on-exec by default.
SCM_RIGHTS raw integers are converted to one managed owner using F_DUPFD_CLOEXEC and the received raw integer is closed.
UnixDescriptor~release returns a caller-owned CLOEXEC duplicate and retires the managed original; transferHandle moves the managed handle itself.
Abandoned UnixDescriptor objects close their still-owned handle.
procedure: Make every ownership transfer explicit; never treat a receipt integer as evidence that two owners may close the same descriptor.

provenance.claim: Architecture defines Foreign Runtime POSIX_FD ownership, SCM_RIGHTS adoption, CLOEXEC duplication, and explicit release/handle transfer.
